groups.name: Describe cloud computing
objectives: Define cloud computing
Describe the shared responsibility model
Define cloud models, including public, private, and hybrid
Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud model
Describe the consumption-based model
Compare cloud pricing models
Describe serverless

groups.name: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
objectives: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud
Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud
Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud
Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud

groups.name: Describe cloud service types
objectives: Describe infrastructure as a service (IaaS)
Describe platform as a service (PaaS)
Describe software as a service (SaaS)
Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type

groups.name: Describe the core architectural components of Azure
objectives: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
Describe availability zones
Describe Azure datacenters
Describe Azure resources and resource groups
Describe subscriptions
Describe management groups

groups.name: Describe Azure compute and networking services
objectives: Compare compute types, including containers, virtual machines, and functions

Describe application hosting options, including web apps, containers, and virtual machines

Describe storage tiers
Describe redundancy options
Describe storage account options and storage types
Identify options for moving files: AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer, Azure File Sync
Describe migration options: Azure Migrate and Azure Data Box

objectives: Describe directory services: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Describe authentication methods: SSO, MFA, passwordless

Describe Azure role-based access control (RBAC)

groups.name: Describe cost management in Azure

Explore the pricing calculator

Describe the purpose of tags

objectives: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview in Azure
Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
Describe the purpose of resource locks

groups.name: Describe features and tools for managing and deploying Azure resources
objectives: Describe the Azure portal
Describe Azure Cloud Shell, Azure CLI, and Azure PowerShell
Describe the purpose of Azure Arc

groups.name: Describe monitoring tools in Azure
objectives: Describe the purpose of Azure Advisor
Describe Azure Service Health

notInObjectives: Azure TCO calculator — not listed in the current skills measured. Treated only as supporting context in Session 18.
Service-level agreements (SLAs) — not a standalone objective; covered only where they support high availability (1.2.1) and cost/service decisions.
Azure support plans — not listed in the current skills measured. Session 24 becomes a mixed-domain final revision instead.
Service Trust Portal — no longer listed; Microsoft Purview (3.2.1) replaces it in Session 20.

sessions.title: Cloud computing fundamentals
Cloud models: public, private, hybrid (and multicloud)
CapEx, OpEx, consumption and pricing models
Benefits of cloud computing and serverless
High availability, scalability, elasticity and agility
Reliability, predictability, security, governance and manageability
Shared responsibility model and IaaS / PaaS / SaaS
Regions, region pairs, sovereign regions, availability zones, datacenters
Resources, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups
Compute: VMs, scale sets, availability sets, Azure Virtual Desktop
Containers: ACI, Container Apps, AKS
App Service, Azure Functions and serverless hosting
Networking: VNets, subnets, peering, DNS, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, endpoints
Storage services, tiers, redundancy, moving files and migration
Data services, storage accounts and hosting choices for data
sessions.note: Databases (SQL Database, Cosmos DB) are not named objectives; this session keeps them to identification level and adds storage-type depth.
